questionBank.name: Information Security Analysts - English bank v1

items.prompt: A payroll API receives a valid login token. What must it still check before returning an employee's payslip?

options.text: Whether the request used the standard page URL
Whether this actor is authorized to read that payslip
Whether the client hid the payroll menu
Whether the token contains a display name

items.prompt: A new API operation has no approved access rule. Under a deny-by-default policy, what is the correct response to a request?

options.text: Allow read access and block writes only
Reject access until an applicable authorization permits it
Allow any authenticated account
Let the browser decide whether to send the request

items.prompt: Employees may read only their own expense reports. Which check enforces this rule for GET /reports/{id}?

options.text: Require the caller to know the report UUID
Require an Accept: application/json header
Compare the report owner with the trusted authenticated actor
Compare the owner with a userId query parameter

items.prompt: A manager may read reports for assigned units but may edit only their own report. How should the service authorize PATCH on another unit member's report?

options.text: Deny all manager reads to avoid separate checks
Allow the edit if the report is already visible on screen
Deny the edit while retaining the permitted read
Allow the edit because the read permission succeeded

items.prompt: An export endpoint queues a worker job. Policy requires both the request and job execution to respect the user's current data access. The user's grant is revoked before the worker starts. What should happen?

options.text: Reauthorize execution and stop the unauthorized export
Use the worker service account's broad access as user consent
Execute because queue admission succeeded earlier
Export first and mark the audit entry as revoked afterward

items.prompt: A tenant-scoped document lookup checks documentId but trusts organizationId supplied by the browser. Which correction enforces tenant isolation?

options.text: Return only the document title for other tenants
Compare two browser-supplied organization fields
Bind the query to the actor's trusted organization and authorized document
Encrypt the response using the same API session

items.prompt: A service caches document-read decisions by actorId. The policy depends on actor, document, tenant and current grant revision. What change prevents one allowed read from authorizing unrelated documents?

options.text: Include all policy inputs and invalidate decisions when grants change
Cache only denials indefinitely
Keep actorId only and shorten cache lifetime to one hour
Add the document's display title to the actor-only key

items.prompt: A bulk download contains ten documents. Policy requires every requested document to be authorized and the batch to fail without output if any is denied. One document belongs to another tenant. Which implementation meets the rule?

options.text: Check permission on the first document only
Stream permitted documents and fail on the first denied one
Drop the foreign document and report success
Authorize the entire set before creating any downloadable output

items.prompt: An endpoint checks access to invoice A, then loads a download object using an independently supplied storage key. What must change to prevent authorization bypass?

options.text: Add another check that invoice A exists
Log both identifiers and continue
Resolve the download object from the authorized invoice association
Validate that the storage key has a UUID shape

items.prompt: A host sends IPv4 traffic to a destination outside its directly connected subnet and has a valid default route. Which next hop normally handles that traffic?

options.text: The configured default gateway
The configured DNS server
Every host on the local subnet
The destination host's local loopback interface

items.prompt: A service is reachable by its known IP address but its host name does not resolve. Which subsystem should be checked first?

options.text: DNS resolution for that host name
The application's account-role table
The service's business data backup schedule
The web page's language setting

items.prompt: Which address is in the same IPv4 /24 subnet as 192.0.2.10/24?
A router has routes 10.0.0.0/8 via G1 and 10.4.0.0/16 via G2. No policy routing is used. Where does it forward a packet for 10.4.8.9?

options.text: Neither gateway because two routes match
Both gateways in round-robin order
G1
G2

items.prompt: DNS returns a CNAME for app.example pointing to service.example. To obtain the IPv4 address, what should the resolver do?

options.text: Request an MX record as the address for every service
Treat the CNAME text itself as an IPv4 address
Resolve the target name's A record
Replace the client's default route with the target name

items.prompt: An authoritative A record changes, but a resolver still holds the old positive answer within its TTL. Why can clients still receive the old address?

options.text: Changing an A record changes no resolver behavior until a host reboot
Every query must bypass cache after any upstream change
The resolver may use its unexpired cached answer
The authoritative server must keep both IPs permanently

items.prompt: A host has a working default route through G1 and a stale 203.0.113.0/24 route through unreachable G2. Ordinary longest-prefix forwarding is used and no failover removes routes. Why can 203.0.113.20 fail while other external addresses work?

options.text: DNS always prefers the longer route
A /24 route applies to all IPv4 destinations
The more-specific stale route wins for that destination
The default route overrides every specific route

items.prompt: After adding a remote subnet, outbound packets arrive at the server but no reply reaches the client. The server has no matching return route or default route. What should be corrected first?

options.text: Change the client's DNS TTL
Duplicate the outbound route on the client only
Increase the application's login timeout indefinitely
Provide an authorized return path to the client's subnet

items.prompt: Routes include 198.51.100.0/24 via G1, 198.51.100.128/25 via G2 and 0.0.0.0/0 via G3. With normal prefix selection and equal policy, which pair is correct for destinations .50 and .200?

options.text: .50 uses G2; .200 uses G1
Both use G2
Both use G3
.50 uses G1; .200 uses G2

items.prompt: What is the purpose of an approved configuration baseline?

options.text: List only changes proposed but never approved
Record the agreed configuration used to control later changes
Store only the names of system administrators
Replace operational monitoring for every component

items.prompt: A firewall rule is changed under an approved ticket. Which record update best preserves traceability?

options.text: Replace the old record with the words 'network updated'
Change the ticket title without recording the rule
Record the implemented rule, approval and resulting baseline version
Keep the ticket open but omit deployment details

items.prompt: Why retain earlier approved baseline versions after a new baseline is deployed?

options.text: To make every earlier version simultaneously current
To allow administrators to bypass later approval
To support historical trace and controlled rollback
To avoid recording the newly deployed configuration

items.prompt: A scan finds a production TLS setting different from the approved baseline, with no change ticket. What is the appropriate record-handling action?

options.text: Mark the old baseline as approved again without investigation
Edit the baseline to match production immediately
Investigate the difference and use change control to resolve and document it
Delete the scan result because the service is healthy

items.prompt: An emergency change process permits immediate containment followed by documented retrospective review. What should its configuration record contain?

options.text: A fabricated earlier approval time
No record until the next regular release
Only a statement that the normal process was skipped
Actual change, reason, actor, timing and required follow-up review

items.prompt: A server inventory records package version 4.1, while authenticated inspection reports 4.3 after an approved patch. How should the discrepancy be resolved?

options.text: Downgrade the recorded version to 4.0 for consistency
Treat every inventory discrepancy as proof of compromise
Close the patch ticket using the old inventory value only
Verify the deployment evidence and update the inventory to the confirmed state

items.prompt: Two approved changes modify the same configuration file from baseline B7. The second deployment overwrites the first. What record and process correction is most appropriate?

options.text: Reconcile the deployed state against both changes and issue a reviewed successor baseline
Label both tickets successful because each had approval
Discard the first ticket so the records match the last deployment
Create two different current baselines for the same environment without scope distinction

items.prompt: A deployment fails and the approved rollback restores B12. The records had already named B13 as current. What is the correct final record?

options.text: Leave B13 current because it was the intended release
Delete B13 and its failure details
Rename B12 to B13 without preserving the difference
Show B12 as the restored current state and retain B13's deployment and rollback history

items.prompt: A fleet report says 100% compliant, but 20 of 100 expected servers supplied no configuration data. What should the configuration record report?

options.text: 100 compliant because no drift was received from the missing servers
Remove the unresponsive servers from the expected inventory
20 noncompliant and 80 omitted
80 observed servers with their results and 20 with unverified state

items.prompt: A service health objective is availability of successful user requests. Which measurement most directly reflects it?

options.text: Number of open feature requests
Size of the source repository
Successful requests divided by all eligible user requests
Total number of deployed servers

items.prompt: An agreed alert triggers when error rate exceeds 2% for five minutes. One sample exceeds 2% for ten seconds. What does that observation alone establish?

options.text: A short spike occurred; the five-minute alert condition is not yet established
The service is permanently healthy
A five-minute outage is confirmed
The threshold should be removed

items.prompt: A health dashboard stops receiving data. What should the operator conclude initially?

options.text: The service is definitely down
The service has zero errors
Monitoring visibility is unknown and the telemetry gap needs investigation
The last green value remains valid forever

items.prompt: A system reports average latency of 80 ms, but users complain about rare multi-second requests. Which added measure best checks the complaint?

options.text: The server purchase price
The lowest observed request latency only
A high latency percentile for the affected request population
A weekly count of code commits

items.prompt: Error alerts start after a release. Database saturation rises at the same time. What is the best next monitoring action?

options.text: Silence all database alerts until users stop complaining
Change the error threshold so the current rate appears healthy
Correlate release timing, request failures and database measurements
Declare the release the confirmed cause solely from timing

items.prompt: A report compares yesterday's 500 errors with today's 700 errors while traffic doubled. Which comparison is needed before concluding reliability worsened?

options.text: Exclude all failed requests from today's traffic count
Compare error rates using consistent request scope and time windows
Assume more errors always mean a higher error rate
Compare repository sizes on the two days

items.prompt: A service has two routes: 99,000 requests at 0.1% errors and 1,000 requests at 20% errors. The overall alert threshold is 1%. How should monitoring address a critical route's hidden failure?

options.text: Remove the low-traffic route from monitoring
Declare both routes healthy because the aggregate is below 1%
Retain the overall view and add scoped route indicators and alerts
Average 0.1% and 20% without traffic weighting as the system rate

items.prompt: An alert evaluates a five-minute success rate. A collector outage removes four minutes of samples, leaving one healthy minute. What is the defensible status?

options.text: Insufficient telemetry for the full window, with a monitoring-gap signal
Five-minute objective failed at 0%
Automatically lower the objective to the observed minute
Five-minute objective met at 100%

items.prompt: CPU is high, queue depth is growing and throughput is flat. The agreed runbook calls for a controlled capacity adjustment when all three persist. What observation best verifies improvement after the adjustment?

options.text: CPU is lower for one sample, regardless of queue growth
More servers appear in the inventory
Queue depth falls while throughput and error/latency indicators return within agreed limits
The alert was manually acknowledged

items.prompt: A server's approved hardening baseline disables an unused remote administration service. What should the operator do?

options.text: Disable every service including required administration
Disable the service and verify required administration still works
Rename the service without changing its configuration
Keep it enabled because unused services cannot be attacked

items.prompt: A patch installer reports success. What should happen before the patch task is treated as verified?

options.text: Assume every fleet member received the patch
Check the deployed version and relevant service/security behavior
Delete the change record immediately
Mark unrelated vulnerabilities resolved too

items.prompt: An application requires one approved exception to a hardening setting. How should it be handled?

options.text: Document and authorize the scoped deviation with its risk and compensating measures
Disable the whole baseline for all servers
Declare the setting unnecessary for every application
Hide the exception from configuration records

items.prompt: A security update requires a reboot, but the old vulnerable process remains running. What is the correct deployment conclusion?

options.text: Any later scan must be a false positive
The vulnerability is resolved because the package downloaded
The reboot requirement can be ignored whenever traffic is high
The remediation is not yet verified effective; complete the required activation and checks

items.prompt: Policy permits database access only from the application subnet. Which hardening verification best checks the firewall change?

options.text: Block the application subnet as well
Verify the application connection succeeds and an unauthorized subnet is blocked
Check only that one authorized client succeeds
Check only that the rule exists in a file

items.prompt: A vendor patch is available for an actively exposed vulnerability, but a compatibility issue appears in the staged rollout. What is the appropriate next action?

options.text: Deploy to every production host without evaluating the issue
Mark the patch complete because staging found the issue
Postpone indefinitely without recording residual risk
Use the approved risk/change process for mitigation or corrected rollout and verify it

items.prompt: A fleet patch job reports 100% success, but authenticated checks find the vulnerable version on 12 hosts. What should the remediation record say?

options.text: The 12 hosts should be removed from inventory
All findings are closed because the job is green
Verified coverage is incomplete; investigate those hosts and keep their findings open
Every host must be reimaged without assessing cause

items.prompt: A hardening change closes an unauthorized port but also breaks an essential approved health check. Which response best meets both security and operations requirements?

options.text: Leave the health check broken because the port is closed
Use change control to restore only the required health-check access and reverify denied access
Allow every network source to use the health-check port
Revert all hardening settings permanently

items.prompt: A critical component has no available patch. An approved temporary rule limits exposure to a trusted gateway. What must the record and verification establish?

options.text: The component can never need further updates
The mitigation is verified merely because it was approved
The vulnerability is permanently fixed by definition
The rule is effective, its remaining exposure is documented, and a replacement/review condition exists

items.prompt: Which statement describes a security risk rather than only an asset or vulnerability?

options.text: A password setting is configured to six characters
The security team has four analysts
An exposed weak password could enable unauthorized payroll changes with financial impact
The organization owns a payroll database

items.prompt: What two dimensions are considered when determining the risk from a threat event?

options.text: The count of slides and report length
Its likelihood and resulting adverse impact
The analyst's job title and tenure
The asset's color and physical size

items.prompt: Before assessing a specific system's risk, why define the assessment scope?

options.text: To replace the need for evidence about threats
To exclude every shared dependency automatically
To guarantee that no unexpected event will occur
To identify the system, boundaries, assumptions and decisions the assessment will support

items.prompt: Two systems share the same vulnerability. One stores public brochures; the other controls payroll approvals. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Declare the public-content system risk-free without checking integrity or availability
Assess impact and exposure in each system's business context
Assign identical organizational risk solely from the shared vulnerability
Use server age as the only prioritization criterion

items.prompt: A team estimates breach likelihood from internet exposure but has not considered an existing effective access control. What is the best refinement?

options.text: Increase impact automatically because a control was deployed
Delete the threat scenario because a control exists
Evaluate how the control changes the relevant likelihood or impact and document evidence
Treat the control's presence as proof of zero risk

items.prompt: An assessment used an assumption that a storage service was internal-only. It is now internet-accessible. What is the appropriate response?

options.text: Erase the earlier report to avoid conflicting assessments
Change every enterprise risk to the highest category
Keep the previous rating until the annual report regardless of change
Reassess the affected scenarios and communicate the changed exposure

items.prompt: An unverified firewall assumption is the main reason a high-impact scenario is rated unlikely. Management must decide on release. What should the analyst communicate?

options.text: Only the high impact and omit the likelihood assumption
A precise near-zero probability without qualification
Treat lack of a prior breach as verification of the firewall
The estimate's uncertainty, the unverified dependency and the evidence needed to reduce uncertainty

items.prompt: A legacy service contains a severe flaw, but its only documented route is through a gateway. Recent inventory suggests an unrecorded alternate route. What is the most defensible risk assessment action?

options.text: Validate reachable paths and reassess the scenario with the uncertainty recorded
Delete the service from scope until the network diagram is fixed
Ignore exposure and use the flaw's severity as the whole organizational risk
Use the gateway diagram as conclusive proof no alternate path exists

items.prompt: A proposed control reduces unauthorized-read likelihood but does not protect availability. The assessed scenario includes both data theft and service interruption. How should the recommendation be framed?

options.text: Describe the covered threat path and remaining availability risk separately
Omit availability from the report so the control appears complete
State that all risks are mitigated because one control was selected
Add the two consequences into a single unsupported probability

items.prompt: A batch service needs read access to one directory and no write access. Which access grant best implements least privilege?

options.text: Write access to every directory
The same permissions as the most privileged human operator
Read access to that directory only
Administrator access to the whole server

items.prompt: The requirement is to detect repeated denied access attempts for analyst review. Which control best addresses it?

options.text: Increase the password field's visual length
Display the policy on the login page only
Encrypt a nightly backup only
Record relevant access events and analyze them against the detection rule

items.prompt: A control is configured to block unauthorized administration. What evidence best verifies its intended protection?

options.text: A screenshot of the control's marketing page
An invoice showing the license is paid
A controlled denied-access check plus a permitted authorized-access check
A statement that no complaints were received

items.prompt: A network firewall restricts access to a web service, but authenticated users must also be limited to their own records. Which control combination meets both requirements?

options.text: Network boundary restrictions plus server-side resource authorization
Network restrictions alone for all user permissions
A hidden menu item instead of either enforcement point
Resource authorization alone while ignoring the required network restriction

items.prompt: Operators must investigate logs but must not alter retained security records. Which permission design fits?

options.text: Deny all investigators any log access
Give log investigators unrestricted deletion rights
Grant scoped log-read access and restrict modification separately
Use one shared administrator login for all investigators

items.prompt: A control passed verification before a major architecture change. What should be done for the changed system?

options.text: Delete every unrelated control result immediately
Treat the earlier pass as permanent certification
Reassess the affected control behavior and update supporting evidence
Approve the change solely because the control is still installed

items.prompt: A rule blocks direct internet access to a database. A review finds an internet-facing proxy that can forward arbitrary database traffic. What verification closes the actual boundary gap?

options.text: Rename the proxy to an internal-service label
Repeat only the direct-port check and close the finding
Assess and restrict the proxy path as well as direct connectivity, then check authorized and denied flows
Document that a firewall exists without checking its scope

items.prompt: A control requires two independent approvals for high-value transfers. The same person can use two role accounts to approve both steps. Which correction best implements the intent?

options.text: Use two different button labels
Enforce independence of approvers by person identity as well as role permissions
Remove approval audit records to prevent account comparison
Require two clicks by the same account

items.prompt: A security control blocks a malicious sample but also blocks every legitimate transaction. The requirement includes protecting the service while allowing approved business use. What is the verification result?

options.text: The legitimate failures can be omitted from the evidence
The control does not yet meet the full requirement
The requirement is met if all users stop using the service
The control is fully effective because the malicious sample was blocked

items.prompt: A worker leaves the organization. According to an approved immediate-offboarding policy, what access action is required?

options.text: Rename the account but keep its permissions
Delete all audit records referring to the person
Keep access active until the password expires
Disable the person's access and revoke applicable credentials or grants

items.prompt: A service account only reads one reporting view. Which assignment is appropriate?

options.text: The minimum read privilege required for that view
Write access to application settings as a precaution
All database-owner permissions
The permissions of the account that created the database

items.prompt: Why use individual accounts for administrators rather than a single shared login?

options.text: To eliminate the need for authorization rules
To ensure every user gets administrator privilege
To remove the need for access reviews
To support individual authorization and accountability

items.prompt: An employee moves from Finance to Sales. Their new role is added but the old payroll-export grant remains. What should the access review do?

options.text: Keep both sets permanently to avoid future access requests
Review the display name only
Remove obsolete Finance access and verify the new approved assignment
Disable all Sales colleagues' accounts

items.prompt: A maintenance contractor needs elevated access for a two-hour approved task. Which configuration best fits?

options.text: Grant access to all unrelated systems for convenience
Grant the required scope with an enforced expiry and auditable use
Provide a permanent shared root password
Record the intended expiry in a note without any revocation mechanism

items.prompt: A policy allows Team A to read a folder and Team B to edit it. A user belongs to both, and the approved policy explicitly combines grants. What is the expected permission?

options.text: No access because dual membership is always invalid
Read only because read is less privileged
Administrator access to the entire file server
Read and edit, subject to any separate applicable restrictions

items.prompt: Policy says a suspended account must immediately lose API access. Existing tokens remain cryptographically valid for an hour. Which design meets that policy?

options.text: Change only the account's display name
Accept all signed tokens until expiry
Check current suspension/revocation state at the protected boundary or use equivalent immediate invalidation
Ask the suspended user to delete their token

items.prompt: A user has no direct export grant but inherits it through a nested group. Policy forbids their department from exporting. What should the administrator verify before closing the access issue?

options.text: Rename the nested group
Remove export access from every department without checking scope
Evaluate effective membership paths, remove the prohibited route and check effective access
Confirm only that the direct-grant list is empty

items.prompt: A privileged-access system requires an approved request and separate approver. An emergency override currently allows the requester to self-approve without review. Which correction preserves a controlled emergency path?

options.text: Apply the approved emergency authorization, time limit, audit and independent follow-up requirements
Keep self-approval permanently for every request
Delete emergency-use logs to protect the operator
Prohibit all emergency access regardless of the approved procedure

items.prompt: An alert reports repeated failed logins. What is the appropriate first analytical step?

options.text: Declare a confirmed breach from the alert title alone
Change every account password before examining scope
Delete the alert because failed logins are common
Inspect relevant authentication events and account context

items.prompt: Why record time zone and clock information when investigating events across systems?

options.text: To replace account and host identifiers
To make log messages shorter
To establish that every event is malicious
To correlate events on a consistent timeline

items.prompt: When should an alert be classified as an incident?

options.text: When analyzed evidence meets the organization's defined incident criteria
Whenever the oldest alert has waited an hour
Only after every affected system has failed
Whenever its dashboard color is red

items.prompt: A new-location login alert occurs during an approved employee trip. Which investigation is most appropriate?

options.text: Confirm compromise solely because the location is new
Correlate travel context with authentication, device and session evidence
Remove location alerts for all employees
Close the alert solely because a trip was approved

items.prompt: A host alert and proxy log show the same unusual destination, but their clocks differ by seven minutes. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Rewrite original logs to make their times match
Treat the events as unrelated solely because timestamps differ
Choose whichever timestamp supports the preferred conclusion
Preserve original times and account for the known offset when correlating

items.prompt: An alert is confirmed as an authorized maintenance activity. What is the appropriate closure record?

options.text: Delete every event from that host
Evidence supporting the benign explanation, scope and any justified detection tuning
Close it with only 'false positive' and no supporting context
Mark all future alerts from the host harmless

items.prompt: Several failed logins are followed by a successful session and a large export from a sensitive account. No approved export is known. What is the best analytical conclusion and next step?

options.text: Review only failed logins and omit the export
State that the export proves a specific named attacker was responsible
Treat the correlated activity as a high-concern scenario, assess scope and escalate under incident criteria
Close the case because the final login succeeded

items.prompt: A detector shows suspected data theft, but the relevant proxy logs expired before collection. What should the investigation report?

options.text: The supported observations, evidence gap, uncertainty and next available corroboration
The full stolen dataset with invented details
No theft occurred because the logs are unavailable
Delete the detector observation because corroboration is incomplete

items.prompt: Two alerts compete for one analyst: repeated blocked scans against a public test host and an active unauthorized privileged session on a payroll system. With no other evidence, which should be prioritized?

options.text: The scan solely because its event count is larger
Neither until a weekly report is available
Whichever alert arrived first regardless of risk
The privileged payroll session because current access and business impact warrant urgent assessment

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: An approved incident procedure calls for isolating an infected endpoint from normal network access. What is the purpose of that action?

options.text: Limit the incident's spread and further damage
Guarantee that all persistence is removed
Prove the malware's original author
Replace the need to preserve incident records

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: Why maintain a chronological incident action log?

options.text: To guarantee a particular legal outcome
To eliminate the need for technical evidence
To preserve who did what, when and why for review and coordination
To publish every incident detail to all employees

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: Before returning a recovered service to normal use, what should the response team verify?

options.text: Only that its login screen has the right logo
Restored operation and the relevant security conditions required by the recovery plan
Only that the incident ticket has an assignee
That all old incident evidence has been deleted

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: A responder must contain a compromised server while preserving available evidence under the approved procedure. Which action fits?

options.text: Copy evidence to an unrestricted public folder
Wipe the server immediately without recording any evidence or action
Leave active unauthorized access indefinitely to avoid changing anything
Use the authorized containment method and record evidence collected and changes made

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: A stolen credential enabled access and the host contains a persistence mechanism. Which response best addresses eradication?

options.text: Delete the alert while leaving the credential and persistence active
Remove the persistence and revoke the compromised access, then verify the affected scope
Restart the host and assume all compromise is gone
Change an unrelated user's password only

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: An analyst is asked to notify an external party during an incident. The plan assigns that communication to a designated lead. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Route verified facts to the designated lead through the approved channel
Post raw evidence publicly before coordination
Invent a confirmed impact number to avoid delay
Wait silently and withhold relevant evidence from the lead

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: A critical server is actively spreading malware. The approved plan permits immediate network isolation, with evidence collection coordinated as feasible. Which action best follows it?

options.text: Wipe all enterprise servers immediately
Disable logging before isolation to reduce disk writes
Delay all containment until a perfect disk image is available
Isolate promptly, preserve feasible evidence and document the decision and resulting changes

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: A service is restored from a clean backup, but the exploited credential is still valid and the vulnerable entry point remains open. What is the recovery decision?

options.text: Restore the same backup repeatedly as the sole long-term remedy
Do not declare the required security recovery complete until those conditions are treated and verified
Declare complete because the backup predates the incident
Delete the backup history to prevent recurrence

items.microSkillName: Execute a security incident response procedure
items.prompt: An incident ended after containment and recovery, but responders discovered that the escalation contact was unreachable and delayed action. What follow-up best improves the procedure?

options.text: Remove escalation from the procedure
Record the lesson, assign corrective ownership and verify an updated escalation method
Rewrite the incident times so no delay appears
Close the issue because the service is currently healthy

items.prompt: Before beginning a technical vulnerability assessment, what must be established?

options.text: Authorized scope, permitted activities and rules of engagement
A list of unrelated organizations to scan too
A guarantee that no weakness will be found
Permission implied only by public network reachability

items.prompt: A scanner reports a possible vulnerability. What is the defensible initial classification?

options.text: A resolved issue because the scanner finished
Proof that every system in the organization is vulnerable
A confirmed compromise by a specific attacker
A finding requiring validation and context

items.prompt: Which information makes a vulnerability finding actionable?

options.text: Only the analyst's preferred deadline without a finding description
Only a red severity icon
Affected asset, observed condition, supporting evidence and potential impact
Only the scanner product's name

items.prompt: A scanner flags a vulnerable software version from a network banner. The supplier backported the fix without changing that banner. What should the assessor do?

options.text: Delete the scan result without retaining the validation basis
Confirm the vulnerability solely from the unchanged banner
Assume all supplier packages are safe without checking the advisory
Check authoritative package/advisory evidence and the relevant condition within authorization

items.prompt: An approved assessment lists subnet A only. Discovery reveals a connected subnet B. What should the assessor do before testing B?

options.text: Assume the owner of A owns every reachable network
Test B because routing allows it
Obtain a scope change or clarification through the agreed authority
Use a more aggressive tool so B finishes quickly

items.prompt: An unauthenticated scan finds no issues on a host, but it could not inspect local packages or configuration. How should the result be reported?

options.text: No findings in the observed coverage, with the uninspected areas stated
Omit the coverage limitation because the scan was successful
Every local package is vulnerable
The host is fully secure

items.prompt: During an authorized production scan, error rates exceed the engagement's stop threshold. What should the assessor do?

options.text: Continue until every target is scanned because scope was approved
Stop the affected activity, notify the agreed contact and follow the recovery/escalation rule
Raise the threshold without approval
Hide the errors because the scanner caused them

items.prompt: A finding applies only when feature F is enabled. Version matches the vulnerable range, but evidence about F is missing. Intrusive exploitation is prohibited. What is the best validation path?

options.text: Confirm the finding solely from version while ignoring F
Mark it resolved solely because exploitation is prohibited
Exploit the service to settle the question despite the prohibition
Use permitted configuration/vendor evidence and record uncertainty if applicability remains unresolved

items.prompt: One critical finding is on an isolated retired host and another high finding affects an exposed payroll API. What should accompany remediation prioritization?

options.text: Validate asset status, exposure and business impact alongside technical severity
Ignore the payroll finding because it is labeled high rather than critical
Delete the retired-host finding without confirming retirement
Sort by scanner severity and forbid any contextual review

items.prompt: A team says a vulnerability is fixed after deploying a patch. Which evidence best supports closure?

options.text: The vulnerability report was archived
The patch ticket has a new assignee
The scanner license was renewed
A relevant verification that the affected deployed condition is resolved

items.prompt: A temporary firewall mitigation reduces access to a vulnerable service. How should its status be described?

options.text: Mitigated exposure with the underlying vulnerability and review condition tracked
Permanently patched
Verified complete solely because the rule was requested
